title: Ha'azinu: the Rock (Deuteronomy 32:4)
hookLine: God is called "The Rock, His work is perfect"

lines: TURN LEFT AT THE BIG ROCK.
cards: Rain soaks in and moves on. Two verses later, the song reaches for the opposite picture: something that doesn't move at all. A great boulder at the edge of a field, or in the middle of a riverbed.
The water goes around it for centuries. People sit on it, lean against it, give directions by it: turn left at the big rock. In Ha'azinu, Moses takes that rock and makes it a name.

teach.b: "The Rock, His work is perfect; For all His ways are justice." The Hebrew is tzur: rock, the solid kind, a cliff face or a boulder. Ha'azinu comes back to the word for God several times.
A rock is what you build on, what you shelter behind, what's still there when everything else washes away.

In the wilderness, rock meant shade and refuge, and twice in the story, even water. Then the song turns the image around. When the people grow comfortable, it says, they scorned the Rock of their salvation.
You can lean on a rock, and you can also forget it's there at all. The picture went deep into Jewish prayer.

At the end of the Amidah, the standing prayer, many people say a verse from the Psalms: "Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer."
And this very verse, the Rock, His work is perfect, opens the prayer called tzidduk hadin, accepting the judgment, said at Jewish funerals, when a family is at its least steady.
In that moment it can be a very hard sentence to say. That may be part of its point. The Rock doesn't promise that everything will feel right.
It names something that stays when nothing else does.

how: The phrase 'the Rock, His work is perfect' opens tzidduk hadin, recited at Jewish burials, and many Jews close the Amidah with Psalm 19:15, 'my Rock, and my Redeemer'.

o: give ear: the name of Moses' last song
the song of the sea: sung after the crossing
hear, O Israel: the Shema's first words

games.q: inside the Rock — tap the pairs.
p: a funeral prayer that opens with the Rock
scorned the Rock of their salvation

s: the Rock appears only once in Ha'azinu
the song returns to it several times.
'The Rock, His work is perfect' is said at Jewish funerals

games.q: the people have grown comfortable and well fed. according to the song, what happens to their relationship with the Rock?
o: they lean on it more than ever.
they forget it and scorn it.
they build a temple on it.
games.why: Deuteronomy 32:15: comfortable, they scorned the Rock of their salvation. you can forget the thing that holds you up.

practice: If there's a stone nearby, pick it up; if not, a mug or a book, anything solid, and feel that it doesn't change while your thoughts and your mood move.
If you pray, you can say the psalm's old words, my Rock, and my Redeemer; if not, simply let your hand rest on something that stays.

wordCard.voice: Ha'azinu. Give ear. And tzur: the Rock, the name the song gives God again and again.

orig.note: Hebrew: rock. a name for God in Ha'azinu, Deuteronomy 32:4.

carryVoice: Your line: the rock. Solid enough to build on, and to lean on. See you tomorrow.
